chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'If a woman disavows her husband, she is one (divorce), and he is a suitor from the suitors.'

key_terms.الْمُبَارَاة: disavowment by payment (a type of divorce initiated by the wife)
key_terms.وَاحِدَةٌ: one (referring to a single, irrevocable divorce)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal effect of a woman initiating disavowment (mubarat) on her marital status and the husband's ability to remarry her?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that in al-mubarat, where the wife initiates the divorce by paying compensation, the ruling is treated as a single irrevocable divorce (talaq wahid). Consequently, the husband does not regain full marital rights immediately but remains in the status of a suitor (khatab), requiring a new marriage contract (aqd) and fresh dowry (mahr) to remarry her, distinguishing it from the standard revocable divorce phase. This ruling underscores the financial and legal weight of the wife's initiative in dissolving the bond under Shia jurisprudence.
